subject.title: [Bug] Sandbox validateEnvVarValue base64 heuristic false-positives on legitimate long alphanumeric values

question: Should OpenClaw narrow the sandbox env credential-data warning so structured base64 values only warn when the env var name looks credential-related?
rationale: The false positive is source-reproducible, but the fix direction changes sandbox credential-warning coverage and needs an explicit security-boundary tradeoff.

options.title: Approve key-aware heuristic
options.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main, port the active skill runtime caller, and land the narrower warning policy with focused validation.

options.title: Keep broader warning coverage
options.body: Require a different heuristic that reduces false positives without relying on credential-like env names.

options.title: Treat broad warnings as intentional
options.body: Close the issue only if maintainers explicitly prefer conservative advisory warnings over false-positive reduction.

recommendation.title: Approve key-aware heuristic
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main, port the active skill runtime caller, and land the narrower warning policy with focused validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sanitizer warning helper and initial tests, making them the best history-backed owner for this policy choice.
